correctness.rationale: The invertible substitutions are exactly the (q−1)q³ choices of nonzero linear and arbitrary higher coefficients. The scalar direction is fixed. On the radical the triangular diagonal is (a,a²,a³,a⁴). Away from ±1 only multipliers of exact order 3 or 4 have a fixed radical coordinate, exactly one. For odd characteristic and a=−1, eliminating the coefficients of t and t³ leaves −2(b²+c)x₂=0 with x₄ free, giving q² dimension-3 maps, and q³−q² dimension-2 maps. At a=1 the first-nonzero coefficient strata b,c,d,none give ranks (3,2,1,0), (2,2,1,0), (2,1,1,0) in the respective characteristic bands; weighting by (q−1)q²,(q−1)q,q−1,1 yields all the stated fibers. Independently one can count orbits by constant term and order of the first nonzero radical term: order 1 gives one, order 2 gives two in odd characteristic or 2q−1 in characteristic two (normalize the square coefficient, then b↦b²+βb has image of index two for β≠0), order 3 gives 1+r₃ except in characteristic three, where it gives q, and order 4 gives gcd(4,q−1). Adding the constant-only orbit per scalar recovers the three Burnside formulas. Independent composition/elimination in /workspace/branches/fe4c77b7-72ca-4498-9b81-cdc434d412a5/replay.py matched every fiber at q=2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,13,16,25, and direct element-orbit enumeration gave 14,27,52 at q=2,3,4. These are finite checks, not the all-field proof.

value.rationale: The full group acting on its own truncated coordinate algebra is a natural finite-field action; the exact spectrum distinguishes more than a group-order or total-orbit calculation. In particular the characteristic-two and characteristic-three fibers isolate different failures of the tame pivot argument, and quantify how they raise orbit growth from order q to order q². Those frequencies and totals are usable benchmarks for longer jets, not consequences of the existing tame count or a renamed characteristic-five result.
